_about: PRO rewrite pass 11: era-3 scenes 79-117 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Massage Therapist
scenarios.text: The team's massage therapist has worked on your legs for years and can tell how your week went by touching your hamstring. They want you to change something.

choices.label: Listen to them
choices.result: You listen to them about everything: sleep, stretching, the way you sit on the plane. Your legs feel younger by midseason.

choices.label: Thank them
choices.result: You thank them publicly at the end of the season, in front of the whole team. They pretend to be annoyed and keep the clip.

choices.label: Book extra sessions
choices.result: You book extra sessions and sleep better than you have in years. Your bank account notices, and your legs are worth it.

scenarios.title: The Old Injury Flares
scenarios.text: An old hip injury flares up on a road trip, in a hotel bed at two in the morning, two days before a game. You can feel it every time you roll over.

choices.label: Tell the trainers right away
choices.result: The trainers, told at breakfast, before it gets worse. They catch it early, and you're fine by Sunday, with a new stretch for life.

choices.label: Work through it quietly
choices.result: Through it, quietly, and the trainers find out later. The hip holds, and it reminds you of itself every morning for a month.

choices.label: Rest it all week
choices.result: No extra kicking all week, ice and rest. It calms down by Saturday, and you miss the work more than you expected.

scenarios.title: The Long Practice Week
scenarios.text: A long week of practice in the August heat, three sessions a day, and your legs feel every one of your years. The rookies are bouncing; you're icing between meetings.

choices.label: Pace yourself
choices.result: Your legs, saved for the kicks that matter. You skip the extra sprints, and you're fresh on Sunday while the rookies limp.

choices.label: Push through every rep
choices.result: Every rep, every sprint, every session, in the heat. Your legs feel it all weekend, and the rookies stop calling you old.

choices.label: Keep the unit laughing
choices.result: Jokes, bad songs and a running bit about the heat. The specialists laugh through the whole week, and it feels shorter.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Retirement Speech
scenarios.text: A teammate's retirement speech, delivered in the locker room with a cracking voice, mentions you by name: 'the kicker who never once let me down'.

choices.label: Hug him afterward
choices.result: A long hug afterward, by his empty locker. Neither of you says much, and you both have to look at the ceiling.

choices.label: Say something back at dinner
choices.result: A few words back, at the team dinner that night, about what he meant to the room. He can't look up from his plate.

choices.label: Keep it with you
choices.result: The words, kept just for yourself. Some nights before big games you think about them, and they steady your hands every time.

scenarios.title: The Team Historian
scenarios.text: The club's historian wants an hour with you for the team archive. She has a recorder, a list of questions and a photo of you as a rookie.

choices.label: Tell every story
choices.result: You tell every story you can remember, including some you probably shouldn't. She laughs until she has to stop the recorder.

choices.label: Tell the true ones
choices.result: You tell the true ones, carefully, including the hard years. She says it's the most honest interview in the archive.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: A short interview, and the archive gets a few good lines. Later you realize you didn't mention the people who got you there.

scenarios.title: The Team's Anniversary
scenarios.text: The club celebrates its fiftieth anniversary with a gala, a banner of club legends across the stadium, and your face is on it, between two Hall of Famers.

choices.label: Meet the old players
choices.result: Players from every era of the club, met one by one at the gala. One of them held for your childhood hero, and he tells you everything.

choices.label: Speak at the event
choices.result: A short speech, on stage, about what the club has meant to you. The old players clap the loudest, and one of them cries.

choices.label: Enjoy it with your family
choices.result: Your family, in the stands, under the banner, quietly. {parent} takes forty photos of your face on the banner, all slightly blurry.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Union Meeting
scenarios.text: The veterans meet about the next labor agreement in a hotel conference room, and it's tense: pensions, health care, the length of the season. Somebody throws a chair.

choices.label: Speak for the specialists
choices.result: The specialists, spoken for, because nobody else was going to. The union adds two lines about kickers to the proposal.

choices.label: Read every clause
choices.result: Every clause of the proposal, read overnight. You find the one about injury guarantees that matters most, and you flag it.

choices.label: Vote with the room
choices.result: Your vote goes with the room, and your opinions stay for the bus. The meeting ends, and nobody throws anything else.

scenarios.title: The Teammate in Rehab
scenarios.text: A teammate goes into a long rehab for a knee injury that may end his career. He's thirty-four and has three kids, and he stops answering texts after the second surgery.

choices.label: Visit him every week
choices.result: Every week, at his house, whether he wants it or not. Some weeks you just watch television together, and some weeks he talks.

choices.label: Keep his locker as it was
choices.result: His locker, kept exactly as it was, with his name on it, at your insistence. The room remembers him every day.

choices.label: Send a message
choices.result: A warm, short message every few weeks. He replies with a thumbs-up months later, and you're glad you kept sending them.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Camp Partner
scenarios.text: A college coach asks you to co-host a kicking camp in July: two hundred high school kickers, three days, a university field and your name on the poster.

choices.label: Co-host it
choices.result: Three days, co-hosted, from dawn to dusk. It's a great week, and five of the kids end up with college scholarships.

choices.label: Bring {holder} along
choices.result: {holder}, recruited to run the holding station. The campers love the two of you together, and {holder} is better with teenagers than you.

choices.label: Pass this year
choices.result: Not this year, you tell the coach. He says the offer stands, and you spend July at the lake with your family.

scenarios.title: The Weekend Away
scenarios.text: A rare weekend away from the city, at a cabin with no neighbors and one bar of signal. Your phone won't stop buzzing anyway: agents, reporters, a teammate's crisis.

choices.label: Turn the phone off
choices.result: Off, in a drawer, for two days. Nothing burns down, and you come back calmer than you've been since August.

choices.label: Check it once a day
choices.result: Once a day, after dinner, for twenty minutes. You answer what matters and let the rest wait, and it works.

choices.label: Answer the teammate
choices.result: The teammate's crisis gets an hour on the porch, on the phone. You lose an afternoon, and he's grateful for years.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Leadership Award
scenarios.text: The club names you its veteran leadership honoree. The award comes with a dinner, a speech, and a young team that will be listening to every word.

choices.label: Accept and speak
choices.result: You accept and talk to the young players about the year you nearly lost your job. The room is silent, and three rookies find you afterward.

choices.label: Share it
choices.result: You bring the specialists up with you and make them stand there while you thank them. {holder} is mortified and delighted.

choices.label: Accept quietly
choices.result: You accept quietly and thank the equipment staff in a handwritten note. They pin it to the wall of the equipment room.

scenarios.title: The Media Feud
scenarios.text: A columnist has a feud with you, nobody knows why, and every column is about you: your age, your contract, your 'declining leg'. {parent} has started writing letters to the editor.

choices.label: Ignore every column
choices.result: Not one column read, not one word said. He runs out of things to say by December and starts writing about the punter.

choices.label: Invite him to practice
choices.result: An invitation to watch practice, from the sideline, for a whole day. The next column is kinder, and he admits you're still good.

choices.label: Put the columns on your garage wall
choices.result: Every column, printed and pinned to the garage wall where you kick. It's very motivating, a little strange, and {parent} adds his letters.

scenarios.title: The Social Media Break
scenarios.text: You take a month off social media after a rough stretch, the apps deleted and the password changed. On day three you keep reaching for a phone that has nothing on it.

choices.label: Stay off the whole month
choices.result: The whole month, off. By week three you stop reaching for your phone, and you read two books and sleep better than in years.

choices.label: Have someone post for you
choices.result: Someone else posts the basics for you: game days, charity events. You don't read the replies, and it's the perfect middle.

choices.label: Spend the time with people
choices.result: The time, spent with real people instead: long dinners, a walk with {best_friend}, an afternoon with {parent}. It's so much better.

scenarios.title: The Charity Ride
scenarios.text: You ride in a charity bike ride across the state with four teammates: three hundred miles, five days, and a support van driven by the equipment manager.

choices.label: Ride with the slowest group
choices.result: The slowest group, the whole way, telling stories. You finish last, laughing, and the charity raises the most it ever has.

choices.label: Ride it hard
choices.result: Hard, every day, at the front. Your legs hate you by day three, and the charity gets a huge photo of you at the finish line.

choices.label: Organize the team's riders
choices.result: The team's riders and the support van, organized by you. Everyone finishes, nobody gets lost, and the equipment manager calls you 'boss'.

scenarios.title: The Coach Who Believed in You
scenarios.text: The coach who gave you your first chance is in the hospital after a heart attack. He's seventy-three, and his wife says he keeps asking about your last game.

choices.label: Visit on your day off
choices.result: A day off, spent at his bedside. He's thin and pale and still giving you notes about your follow-through, which makes you laugh.

choices.label: Call his family
choices.result: His family, called, to ask what would actually help. You do all of it, including fixing his porch steps yourself on a Sunday.

choices.label: Send a long letter
choices.result: A long letter, handwritten over two nights, about everything he did for you. His wife reads it to him, twice, and he keeps it.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Kid
scenarios.text: A teammate's ten-year-old wants to kick and asks you for lessons, very formally, in a handwritten letter he delivers to your locker himself, wearing a tie.

choices.label: Teach him every Saturday
choices.result: Saturday mornings, all fall, on the practice field. He's good, and so is his smile, and his father watches from the fence every week.

choices.label: Make it a family thing
choices.result: Your family and his, together every Saturday: kicking first, then pancakes. The two families become very close over the season.

choices.label: Give one lesson and cleats
choices.result: One proper lesson and a pair of cleats, signed. He wears the cleats to bed for a month and to school for another.

scenarios.title: The Neighbor's Kid
scenarios.text: The neighbor's kid practices kicking in the street every day after school, against a recycling bin, with a ball that's lost most of its air.

choices.label: Show him one thing
choices.result: One thing, shown from the curb: the plant foot. He does it right the next day, and waves at your window.

choices.label: Set up a net in your driveway
choices.result: A net in your driveway, with a new ball, and a sign that says it's his. His mother brings you cookies.

choices.label: Watch from the window
choices.result: From your kitchen window, every afternoon, you watch him kick against the recycling bin and remember, exactly, what it was like being that kid.

scenarios.title: Running the Music
scenarios.text: You've been the locker room DJ for six years, and a rookie wants the job. He has a speaker the size of a refrigerator and opinions about your playlists.

choices.label: Hand it over with a speech
choices.result: The aux cord, handed over with a ceremony and a speech about responsibility. The room cheers, and he plays your favorite song first.

choices.label: Share the job
choices.result: Fridays are his, the rest are yours. It works, and his Fridays are better than you would ever admit out loud.

choices.label: Make him earn it
choices.result: A month of proving himself, playlist by playlist. His is better, and you admit it in front of the whole team meeting.

scenarios.title: The Middle-Aged Rookie
scenarios.text: A thirty-year-old rookie kicker joins the club after years of tryouts, day jobs and empty stadiums at midnight. Everyone keeps saying you two should talk.

choices.label: Talk to him
choices.result: You talk to him over lunch. He spent six years kicking at midnight in a high school stadium, and you leave the table humbled.

choices.label: Help him
choices.result: You help him learn the league: travel, routines, which coaches mean what. He's grateful and fast, which makes you nervous.

choices.label: Stay focused
choices.result: Polite, and focused on your job. He's still competition, whatever his story is, and his story won't keep your job for you.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Seminar
scenarios.text: The union holds a retirement seminar on a Tuesday night. You sit in the back row, near the door, in case you want to leave.

choices.label: Take notes
choices.result: Notes, pages of them, in the back row. Some of it scares you, usefully, and you call your advisor on the drive home.

choices.label: Bring a teammate
choices.result: You bring a teammate who needs it more than you do. He doesn't say a word all night and asks for your notes the next day.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: You leave at the break. Not yet. In the parking lot, you sit in the car a while before you start it.

scenarios.title: The Lost Season
scenarios.text: A season where nothing goes right: the team loses nine straight, the coach is on the hot seat, and your own kicks feel like someone else's.

choices.label: Keep working
choices.result: You keep working, because it's all you can do. By December your kicks feel like yours again, even if the team doesn't.

choices.label: Hold the room together
choices.result: The room, held together while the losses pile up. The young players remember who stayed calm, long after the season.

choices.label: Lean on home
choices.result: Home, every night: dinner with people who don't care about the score. It saves your season, and maybe more than that.

scenarios.title: The Comeback Practice
scenarios.text: After a rough week, you have the best practice of your career: every kick perfect, every hold perfect, and the coaches stop talking to watch.

choices.label: Write down what changed
choices.result: Everything that changed, written down that night: the sleep, the warmup, the one thought. You keep the page in your bag for years.

choices.label: Thank the unit
choices.result: The unit, thanked before you leave the field, one by one. {holder} grins all the way back to the locker room.

choices.label: Go home happy
choices.result: Home, happy, and ten hours of sleep for the first time in a month. You don't analyze any of it.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Who Took Your Spot in College
scenarios.text: The kicker who beat you for a scholarship in college, the one whose name you used to say like a curse, is out of football now and asks for your help finding work.

choices.label: Help him find work
choices.result: Calls to people you know, for him, over a week. A job comes through, and he's grateful, and so, strangely, are you.

choices.label: Make one call
choices.result: One call, for him, to a friend in sales. It turns into a job interview, and he sends you a long message afterward.

choices.label: Wish him well
choices.result: Good luck, said sincerely, and meant. It's strange how small the old wounds look now, and you sleep well that night.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Dinner
scenarios.text: You host the captains for dinner at your house, and it turns into a three-hour argument about the season: the coaches, the quarterback, the losing streak.

choices.label: Steer it to a plan
choices.result: By dessert, a plan: three things to fix, written on a napkin. The captains leave with a purpose, and the season turns.

choices.label: Let it run
choices.result: Three hours of everyone saying everything that needed saying. The room is closer for it, and the dishes take an hour.

choices.label: Take notes for the coaches
choices.result: Notes, taken quietly all night, and the best ideas brought to the coaches the next morning, without anyone's name on them.

scenarios.title: The Booster's Favor
scenarios.text: A wealthy booster asks you to make a few appearances at his business, on his schedule, for a private thank-you. It isn't quite against the rules.

choices.label: Say no politely
choices.result: You say no politely. He doesn't call again, and you never have to wonder what the thank-you would have cost.

choices.label: Ask {coach} first
choices.result: You ask {coach} before answering. The coach says no for you, and you're relieved to have someone else to blame.

choices.label: Do the favor
choices.result: You do the favor. It's fine, technically, and the parties are fun. Then he calls again, and again, and it's harder to say no each time.

scenarios.title: The Team Doctor's Advice
scenarios.text: The team doctor suggests, over coffee, that you start planning your body's next twenty years, not just this season. She has a folder, and it's labeled with your name.

choices.label: Make the plan with her
choices.result: The plan, made with the doctor: stretching, scans, and a word you've never used before, 'longevity'. It's sobering and comforting.

choices.label: Focus on this season
choices.result: This season first, you tell her. The folder goes in your locker, and you think about it more than you admit.

choices.label: Bring family to the appointment
choices.result: {parent} comes to the next appointment and asks the questions you were afraid to. You leave with a plan and a calmer heart.

scenarios.title: The Kicker in the Stands
scenarios.text: A retired kicker you admired as a kid is in the stands, watching you warm up. You recognize the walk before you see the face, and your stomach flips.

choices.label: Go say hello
choices.result: Over to the railing to say hello. He knows your name, your stats and the one kick you'd rather forget, and he laughs about it kindly.

choices.label: Give him a show in warmups
choices.result: The best warmup of your year, for an audience of one. He nods once from the stands, and you feel twelve.

choices.label: Stay in your routine
choices.result: Your routine, unchanged. Afterward he leaves you a short note at the equipment window: 'Good habits.' You keep it for years.

scenarios.title: The National List
scenarios.text: Your name is on the national list for the league's best kicker, and the team's PR staff has eleven interview requests on a whiteboard, color-coded by urgency.

choices.label: Do all eleven
choices.result: All eleven, in a week. Your face is everywhere, you say the same three things forty times, and you sleep badly.

choices.label: Pick three and do them well
choices.result: Three interviews, chosen carefully and done well. One of them becomes the definitive piece about you, the one people still quote.

choices.label: Do none and keep kicking
choices.result: None at all. You keep kicking, the PR staff sighs and erases the whiteboard, and the list says what it says without your help.

scenarios.title: The Skills Contest
scenarios.text: The league invites you to the long-distance contest at the all-star week: a stadium, a television audience, and nine of the strongest legs in the league.

choices.label: Train for it like a playoff
choices.result: Two weeks of training for one contest. You go, compete hard, and come home with a trophy shaped like a goalpost.

choices.label: Go for the fun
choices.result: The week, spent with kickers from every club: dinners, card games, stories. You finish fourth and have the best time of anyone.

choices.label: Decline and rest your leg
choices.result: A polite decline, and your leg gets a week of rest. The contest happens without you, and you watch it from your couch, cheering.

scenarios.title: Loyalty or the Paycheck
scenarios.text: Another club would pay you double, your agent says, with the offer in writing. This one gave you your first chance when nobody else would. The general manager is waiting for your call.

choices.label: Stay
choices.result: You stay. The club remembers it, the locker room remembers it, and so do you, every time you drive past the old stadium.

choices.label: Explore it
choices.result: Your agent explores the offer, fully and openly. You kick the season like a free agent, and the club starts calling more often.

choices.label: Ask your club to match
choices.result: Your club, asked to come closer to the other offer. They meet you partway, and you sign, a little richer and still at home.

scenarios.title: Broke at Thirty-Three
scenarios.text: The money's gone faster than the career. There's a mortgage, a family, a car payment, and maybe three seasons left in your leg, if you're very lucky.

choices.label: Make a hard plan
choices.result: An honest advisor and a hard plan: a smaller house, no new cars, a budget taped to the fridge. It hurts, and it works.

choices.label: Tell your family everything
choices.result: You tell your family everything at the kitchen table. It's the worst conversation of your life and the best one; nobody leaves.

choices.label: Kick for one more contract
choices.result: You decide to kick for one more contract like your family depends on it. It does, and every practice feels heavier.

scenarios.title: The Awards Show
scenarios.text: The league's awards show wants you on the red carpet the night before a practice you can't miss. There's a tuxedo waiting at your hotel and a car at seven.

choices.label: Walk the carpet and leave early
choices.result: The carpet, two interviews and gone before dessert. You make practice on time the next morning, tired and secretly pleased.

choices.label: Ask {coach}
choices.result: {coach} says go, and be on time. You are, at six in the morning, with makeup still behind your ear.

choices.label: Watch from home
choices.result: The awards, watched from home in sweatpants. You cheer loudly for the punter who wins, and you're asleep by ten.

scenarios.title: Someone New, Later
scenarios.text: Years after it ended, a friend's dinner party seats you next to someone who doesn't care about football at all, has never heard of you and wants to talk about birds, of all things.

choices.label: Ask for their number
choices.result: Their number arrives before dessert, written on a napkin with a drawing of a heron. By spring you know more about birds than kicking, almost.

choices.label: Call {best_friend} first
choices.result: {best_friend} listens to the whole story on the drive home and says only, 'Call them.' You don't, yet, but you keep the napkin on your fridge.

choices.label: Not ready yet
choices.result: A lovely evening, and a polite goodbye at the door. You're not ready yet, and you're honest enough with yourself to know it, which feels like progress.

scenarios.title: The Second Wedding
scenarios.text: Married before, both of you. Somewhere between the dishes and the dog, you start talking about doing it again with {love_interest}: smaller, quieter, and somehow harder to plan than the first time.

choices.label: The courthouse and a long dinner
choices.result: A Tuesday at the courthouse, two witnesses, and a long dinner after. Nobody posts anything. It's the happiest day you've had in years, and it belongs only to you.

choices.label: Invite the people who stayed
choices.result: Only the people who stayed through everything: {parent}, {sibling}, {best_friend}. Forty chairs in a backyard, and {sibling} gives a toast that makes everyone cry.

choices.label: Wait one more season
choices.result: One more season, you agree, until you're both sure. {love_interest} understands, mostly, and the conversation comes back every few weeks, a little shorter each time.

scenarios.title: The Anniversary
scenarios.text: Ten years married, and you're in a hotel room in a city you can't remember the name of, with a road game tomorrow. {love_interest} is home with the dog and a cake.

choices.label: Fly {love_interest} in
choices.result: A ticket for the last flight in, booked from the team bus. One night together in a strange city, and it's the best anniversary yet.

choices.label: Plan the real celebration
choices.result: The real celebration, planned for the bye week, down to the restaurant and the song. You talk about it all night on the phone.

choices.label: Call for an hour
choices.result: An hour on the phone from the hotel, talking about the first year: the tiny apartment, the bad car. It's enough, almost.

scenarios.title: The Comeback Year
scenarios.text: Last year everyone wrote your obituary: released, or benched, and called finished in print. This year you're the first one on the field every single morning.

choices.label: Be first every day
choices.result: First on the field and last off it, every day. By September nobody is writing obituaries, and the columnist who wrote the worst one apologizes.

choices.label: Bring the young players
choices.result: The young players, invited to your early sessions. It becomes a club, and the club becomes the core of the team.

choices.label: Prove it with numbers
choices.result: Every kick, charted, and the curve left on {coach}'s desk every Friday. The numbers do all the arguing for you, quietly.

scenarios.title: Who Am I Without It
scenarios.text: A sleepless night at three in the morning, the question you've been avoiding finally sitting on your chest: if you're not the kicker, who are you?

choices.label: Wake {love_interest}
choices.result: {love_interest}, woken gently, and you talk until dawn. By morning you have half an answer and a much fuller heart.

choices.label: Write it all down
choices.result: Everything you are besides a kicker, written on a legal pad. The list is longer than you thought, and some of it surprises you.

choices.label: Walk until it's light
choices.result: A walk at three in the morning, through an empty neighborhood. The question comes with you, and so does the sunrise.

scenarios.title: The Family Vacation
scenarios.text: A real family vacation, a whole week, no phones, and a family that's not used to having you around for seven straight days. The kids keep asking when you're leaving.

choices.label: Be completely there
choices.result: The phone, in a drawer, all week. You build sandcastles, lose at board games and fall asleep on the beach, and everyone notices.

choices.label: Plan every day
choices.result: Every day planned: the boat, the museum, the hike. It's fun and a little exhausting, and the kids love the boat.

choices.label: Train every morning
choices.result: Every morning, a run and a kicking session before anyone wakes up. You're there for the rest, mostly, and {love_interest} notices the mornings.

scenarios.title: The Fan Convention
scenarios.text: A fan convention wants you for a signing weekend. The line includes people who've followed you since high school, and one woman has your peewee league photo.

choices.label: Talk to every person
choices.result: Every person in line gets a real conversation. It takes nine hours, and the woman with the peewee photo cries.

choices.label: Keep the line moving kindly
choices.result: The line, kept moving, with every name said back to them. It's efficient and warm, and you finish on time.

choices.label: Do one day
choices.result: One day of signing, and the other at the hotel pool. The organizers are gracious, and you come home rested.
